newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian voters lose faith in politicians - poll.
newsitem.headline: Colombian voters lose faith in politicians - poll.

text.p: Colombian voters are losing faith in their politicians and most oppose President Ernesto Samper's economic and defence policies, according to a Gallup poll published on Monday.
Samper, dogged by allegations that he financed his winning 1994 election campaign with drug money, has seen his unpopularity rating grow by eight percent in the past year.

Compared to this time last year, seven percent more of those surveyed say they now oppose Chief Prosecutor Alfonso Valdivieso, who has led an anti-corruption crusade against Samper and other officials.
However, Valdivieso still enjoys 57 percent voter support, compared to 33 percent for Samper.
Despite the political scandal surrounding Samper, more of those polled still prefer him to his 1994 election rival, Andres Pastrana of the conservative New Democratic Force.
Of 1,000 adults surveyed in Colombia's four main cities, Bogota, Cali, Medellin, and Barranquilla, 60 percent said they disliked Pastrana and just 29 percent said they supported him.

More than 80 percent of those questioned in the poll, which has a margin of error of 3.5 percent and was broadcast by the RCN radio network, said they opposed the way Samper's government was handling inflation and unemployment.

September figures showed a 3.4 point rise in urban unemployment to 12.1 percent, compared to 8.7 percent in the same month last year. Inflation is running at 18.4 percent, ahead of the 17 percent target set by government for the end of September.
More than three-quarters of those polled disapproved of Samper's strategy to combat Colombia's leftist guerrillas.
At least 150 security force members have died in clashes since late August and 60 soldiers taken prisoner two months ago by the Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia have not been freed.
